questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 : 3**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• Given the ratio **A : B : C = 3 : 4 : 5**, we can assume the values of the variables to be **A = 3k**, **B = 4k**, and **C = 5k**, where k is a non-zero constant.

• The problem asks for the ratio of **√(A² + B²)** to **√(C² − B²)**.

• First, calculate the value of the first term:

**√(A² + B²)** = √((3k)² + (4k)²)

= √(9k² + 16k²)

= √(25k²) = **5k**.

• Next, calculate the value of the second term:

**√(C² − B²)** = √((5k)² − (4k)²)

= √(25k² − 16k²)

= √(9k²) = **3k**.

• The required ratio is **5k : 3k**. Since k is a common factor in both terms, it can be cancelled out, resulting in the simplified ratio **5 : 3**.

• Therefore, the expression **√(A² + B²) : √(C² − B²)** simplifies to **5 : 3**, which corresponds to **Option 3**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Ratio and Proportion**: A ratio is a way of comparing quantities of the same kind by division. When values are given in a ratio like 3 : 4 : 5, they can be treated as absolute values (3, 4, 5) for homogeneous expressions because the common multiplier cancels out.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 ∶ 4. If the sum of these two numbers is 70, then what is their LCM?

⇒ 7x = 70

**LCM of 30 and 40:**

30 = 2 × 3 × 5

40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5

Therefore, LCM of 30 and 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

questions.question: The salaries of P and Q together amount to Rs. 6,40,000. P and Q save 60% and 40%, respectively, of their individual salaries. If their expenditures are the same, then what is the ratio of P's salary to Q's salary?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Expenditure %** of P = 100% − 60% = 40%

**Expenditure %** of Q = 100% − 40% = 60%

Given: Expenditure of P = Expenditure of Q

⇒ 40% of **Salary P** = 60% of **Salary Q**

⇒ Salary P / Salary Q = 60 / 40 = 3 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Salary (P + Q) = ₹6,40,000

Savings of P = 60% | Savings of Q = 40%

Expenditure of P = Expenditure of Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78d9403b3de26ed6ac7a294c5d3c6f49e4392c73167a2d504314b0212260c999.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P be the salary of P and Q be the salary of Q.

⇒ Expenditure of P = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 60% = 40% of P

⇒ Expenditure of Q = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 40% = 60% of Q

⇒ According to the question: 40% × P = 60% × Q

⇒ (40/100) × P = (60/100) × Q

⇒ 40 × P = 60 × Q

⇒ P / Q = 60 / 40

questions.question: A 228 m long train is running at 125 km/h. In what time (in seconds), will it pass a man running at 17 km/h in the same direction in which the train is going?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in same direction = 125 − 17 = 108 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 108 × (5/18) = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s.

**Time taken** = Train Length ÷ Relative Speed = 228 ÷ 30 = 7.6 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.6 sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **train** = 228 m

Speed of **train** (V₁) = 125 km/h

Speed of **man** (V₂) = 17 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/769ef146bbb605bc205672cc974117dc18750830209f8dabde095afd68d14f57.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = Speed of Train − Speed of Man

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 125 − 17 = 108 km/h

⇒ To convert km/h to m/s: 108 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s

⇒ Distance to be covered = Length of train = 228 m

⇒ Time = 228 ÷ 30

⇒ Time = 7.6 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 7.6 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is found by **subtracting** the slower speed from the faster speed (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move toward each other or in opposite directions, the relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance for Crossing

When a train crosses a **man, pole, or tree**, the distance is the length of the train. If it crosses a **platform or bridge**, distance = Length of train + Length of platform.</p

questions.question: Arin alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and Selvi alone can do the same in 8 days. Arin and Selvi undertook to do it for Rs. 7,200. With the help of Kevin, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to Kevin?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Arin alone can do a piece of work in 6 days.

Selvi alone can do the same in 8 days.

Arin and Selvi undertook to do it for Rs. 7,200.

With the help of Kevin, they completed the work in 3 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by Arin in 1 day = 1/6

Work done by Selvi in 1 day = 1/8

Work done by Arin and Selvi together in 1 day = (1/6) + (1/8) = 7/24

Work done by Arin and Selvi together in 3 days = (7/24) × 3 = 7/8

Work done by Kevin in 3 days = 1 - 7/8 = 1/8

Amount to be paid to Kevin = (1/8) × 7,200 = Rs. 900

**∴ The amount to be paid to Kevin is Rs. 900.**

questions.question: A man goes from his house to a vegetable market at the speed of 15 km/h and walked back at the speed of 10 km/h. If the whole journey took 2 hours 30 minutes, find the distance from his house to the vegetable market (in km),

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km.**

questions.question: If 11th June 1987 is Thursday. then what will be the day of the week on 4th Dec 1989?
questions.solution:
Given: **11th June 1987 was Thursday.**

Now,

1987 to 1989 = 2 Years (1 Ordinary Year and 1 Leap Year).

So, 1 Leap Year has 2 odd days,

And, 1 Ordinary Year has 1 odd day.

Total odd days = 2 + 1 = 3.

then, 11th June 1989 will be Thursday + 3 = Sunday.

Now, the number of days between 11th June 1989 to 4th Dec 1989

= 19(June) + 31(July) + 31(August) + 30(September) + 31(October) + 30(November) + 4(December) = 176 days.

= 176 days → 176/7 = 25 week and 1 odd day.

So, **4th Dec 1989** will be Sunday + 1 = Monday.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phillips curve**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Phillips curve** examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes.
 
• It suggests that there is an inverse relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of inflation in an economy.
 
• The curve was introduced by economist A.W. Phillips in 1958, based on empirical data from the United Kingdom.
 
• According to the Phillips curve, lower unemployment in an economy is associated with higher rates of wage inflation.
 
• Conversely, higher unemployment is associated with lower rates of wage inflation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indifference Curve**

 
 
• Can be caused by **changes in consumer preferences, income levels, prices of related goods, and more**. A rightward shift indicates an increase in demand, while a leftward shift indicates a decrease.
 
• An indifference curve represents a graph showing different combinations of two goods that provide the same level of satisfaction or utility to a consumer
 
• Indicates that as a consumer consumes more of one good, they must consume less of the other to maintain the same utility level.
 
• Reflects the diminishing marginal rate of substitution; consumers are willing to give up fewer units of one good to obtain additional units of another good as they have more of it.
 
• Curves that are further from the origin represent higher levels of satisfaction.
 
 
 
• **Supply Curve**
 
 
• A supply curve illustrates the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity of that good that producers are willing to supply.
 
• Indicates that as prices increase, suppliers are willing to offer more of the good, reflecting the profit motive.
 
• Can occur due to factors such as changes in production costs, technology, or number of suppliers. A rightward shift indicates an increase in supply, while a leftward shift indicates a decrease.
 
 
 
• ** Demand Curve**
 
 
• A demand curve shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded by consumers.
 
• Reflects the law of demand, which states that as prices decrease, the quantity demanded increases, and vice versa.
